title: Mutation probe that RAISED a loop cap turned an O(n) repair into O(n^2) and hung for 10 minutes
impact: One 600s tool timeout, ~10 minutes of a core pinned, and 9095 leaked files left in %TEMP% from a TemporaryDirectory that never got to clean up. No repo damage: the mutated file was restored by hand and the temp tree removed after confirming every file in it was the fixture's.
cause: Proving a bound by raising it assumes the loop body is O(1). Mine was not: each attempt re-globbed the ADR directory, so cost grew with attempts and 10000 attempts became 10000 globs over a directory that had also grown to 10000 files. I chose 10000 to avoid an infinite loop and got quadratic growth instead, which is the same hazard wearing a different number.
guard: The cap case asserts an INDEPENDENT ceiling (new_adr.MAX_ALLOCATE_ATTEMPTS <= 10) rather than reading the constant back, so the mutation proving it can be 11 - over the ceiling, small enough that the quadratic term is trivial. A probe that must be chosen before the loop is measured is how this happened; measure the body's cost per iteration first.

title: An agent abandoned a three-file refactor mid-split, leaving an extends a base class that was never committed, and main did not compile for every other agent
impact: item_workbench_app.gd declared `extends ItemWorkbenchBody` while item_workbench_body.gd was untracked. Any clean checkout or cold import failed with 'Could not resolve class ItemWorkbenchBody', and because a parse error aborts suite loads process-wide it reddened every suite that boots the app: world_stage went to 4 passed / 37 failed, and clan, combat and quest suites went red for reasons outside their own slice. The work was good - a documented three-file split for a file over both the 1000-line ceiling and the 20-method cap - and 45 minutes of it was unrecoverable to anyone who did not write it.
cause: A refactor was dispatched to split item_workbench_app.gd into ItemWorkbenchPlay (clocks), ItemWorkbenchBody (hero and attaches) and ItemWorkbenchReadout (combat readout), and the agent hit its turn limit partway through. The shell's new `extends` line was committed by a DIFFERENT agent sweeping the tree while the base class it named stayed untracked. Nothing in the toolchain noticed: arch reads source references and the base file existed on disk, and the class is only resolved at Godot compile time. This is INC-0004's recurrence with a new shape - the lost work was not reverted, it was never committed, and the partial state was WORSE than either end because it was unreachable from both.
guard: A split that introduces a new `extends` is not committable until every class in the chain is tracked. The cheap check that would have caught it: after committing an `extends`, run uv run python -m tools test --suite <anything that boots the app> and read the FIRST parse error rather than the 37 assertions it caused. A parse error in one file aborts suite loads process-wide, so a large red count is nearly always ONE unparseable file - attribute it before touching anything else (this is INC-0014's rule and it held). The durable guard is a reachability check in tools/arch: for every `extends SomeClass`, assert game/src/**/some_class.gd is tracked.

title: A three-deep inheritance chain (App -> Readout -> Body) that Godot will not resolve
impact: Four suites cannot mount the real scene: rebirth_play_wiring (1/10), creation_play_wiring, soul_hearth, creation_reachability. Harmless elsewhere - suites that do not load the composition root pass: soul_death_loop 43/0, soul_arrival_ladder 30/0, soul_death_world_fact, save_envelope 144/0, save_round_trip 73/0.
cause: A concurrent agent split ItemWorkbenchApp into item_workbench_readout.gd (extends ItemWorkbenchBody) and item_workbench_play.gd, with item_workbench_app.gd extending ItemWorkbenchReadout. Both new files exist, both parse under gdformat, both carry class_name, and after DELETING global_script_class_cache.cfg and forcing a full reimport the cache is rebuilt WITH the ItemWorkbenchReadout entry - and Godot still reports 'Could not resolve class ItemWorkbenchReadout'. The split has since committed and gone quiet, so this is not a half-write: it is a real three-deep chain the build will not resolve.
guard: Deleting global_script_class_cache.cfg and forcing a reimport is the diagnostic that separates a stale cache from a real defect. The cache listed the class AND Godot still refused it, which is what proved the split was at fault. Do not repeat the reimport.
